originalTitle: Asian stocks slide as AI selloff deepens, U.S. tariff threats weigh on sentiment
summary: Investing.com -- Most Asian stocks fell on Wednesday as renewed selling in technology shares erased much of the previous session's AI-driven rebound, with fresh U.S. tariff threats and concerns over the returns from artificial-intelligence investments further undermining risk appetite. Treasuries gained as investors sought safer assets.
content:
Investing.com -- Most Asian stocks fell on Wednesday as renewed selling in technology shares erased much of the previous session's AI-driven rebound, with fresh U.S. tariff threats and concerns over the returns from artificial-intelligence investments further undermining risk appetite. Treasuries gained as investors sought safer assets.

Taiwan's Weighted Index dropped 7.4%, while South Korea's KOSPI fell 6%. Nasdaq 100 futures lost 1.3% and S&P 500 futures declined 0.7% in Asian trade. Hong Kong's Hang Seng bucked the regional trend, rising 0.6%.

Wall Street ended mixed on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 falling 0.5% and the Nasdaq Composite losing 1.5%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.9%.

Nvidia fell 5.9% after Monday's 31% surge, while Anthropic slipped below its IPO price. Dell and HP shares edged higher in extended trading after issuing upbeat forecasts, with Dell gaining 4.1% following stronger-than-expected results tied to AI server demand.

The retreat followed reports that the Trump administration was preparing to release findings of a probe into alleged excess industrial capacity among 16 major trading partners, including China and the European Union. The investigation could pave the way for additional tariffs, forming part of Washington's effort to replace broader duties struck down by the Supreme Court.

Investors are also awaiting Wednesday's U.S. core PCE inflation figures, which could influence expectations for a December Federal Reserve rate increase.

Asian markets retreat as chip-heavy exchanges lead losses

MSCI's Asia-Pacific equities gauge fell 2.7%, while the MSCI All Country World Index slipped 0.4%.

Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 3.3% while TOPIX lost 1%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 declined 0.4%, New Zealand's NZX 50 gained 0.7% and Singapore's Straits Times Index slipped 0.2%.

China's CSI 300 and Shanghai Composite fell 0.88% and 0.98%, respectively. India's Gift Nifty 50 futures down 0.2%.

Meanwhile, Australian inflation accelerated to 4.9% in October, with trimmed mean inflation rising to 3.8% and exceeding expectations, even as RBA official David Jacobs described financial conditions as restrictive following five rate hikes that lifted the cash rate to an 18-year high of 4.85%.

Brent crude fell 1.2% to around $90.30 a barrel as traders weighed rising supply against escalating attacks on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz.

Alibaba subsidiary blacklisting adds to regional AI supply-chain concerns

Chipmakers bore the brunt of the renewed selling. SK Hynix fell 9.1%, Samsung Electronics lost 9.3% and LG Innotek declined 5.5%. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. dropped 7.6%, Foxconn fell 9.2% and Largan Precision lost 1.4%. Japan's Kioxia plunged 15%, while Murata fell 16.1%.

Chinese technology shares were also weaker, with Naura Technology down 8.5%, Cambricon Technologies losing 3.7% and Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp. declining 2.6%. Z.AI and MiniMax fell 8.5% and 7.1%, respectively.

The U.S. Commerce Department also added seven Southeast Asian entities, including Alibaba's Singapore subsidiary Apex Enterprise Solutions, to its export-control blacklist over concerns about potential diversion of advanced computing products.

Alibaba called the listing erroneous, denied that Apex had diverted controlled chips and said it would pursue legal options.

The move could complicate access to advanced computing infrastructure for regional cloud and AI operators, while increasing scrutiny of intermediaries involved in cross-border semiconductor supply chains.

chineseTitle: 随着 AI 抛售加剧，亚洲股市下滑，美国关税威胁打压市场情绪
chineseSummary: Investing.com——周三大多数亚洲股市下跌，科技股再次抛售，抹去了前一交易日人工智能驱动的反弹的大部分内容，美国新的关税威胁和对人工智能投资回报的担忧进一步削弱了风险偏好。由于投资者寻求更安全的资产，国债上涨。
chineseContent:
Investing.com——周三大多数亚洲股市下跌，科技股再次抛售，抹去了前一交易日人工智能驱动的反弹的大部分内容，美国新的关税威胁和对人工智能投资回报的担忧进一步削弱了风险偏好。由于投资者寻求更安全的资产，国债上涨。

台湾加权指数下跌7.4%，韩国综合股价指数下跌6%。在亚洲交易中，纳斯达克 100 指数期货下跌 1.3%，标准普尔 500 指数期货下跌 0.7%。香港恒生指数逆势上涨 0.6%。

华尔街周二收盘涨跌互现，标准普尔 500 指数下跌 0.5%，纳斯达克综合指数下跌 1.5%，道琼斯工业平均指数上涨 0.9%。

Nvidia 在周一飙升 31% 后下跌 5.9%，而 Anthropic 则跌破 IPO 价格。戴尔和惠普在发布乐观预测后，股价在盘后交易中小幅走高，其中与人工智能服务器需求相关的强于预期的业绩使戴尔股价上涨 4.1%。

此前有报道称，特朗普政府正准备公布对中国和欧盟等 16 个主要贸易伙伴涉嫌工业产能过剩的调查结果。这项调查可能为额外关税铺平道路，成为华盛顿取代最高法院取消的更广泛关税的努力的一部分。

投资者还在等待周三公布的美国核心PCE通胀数据，该数据可能会影响对美联储12月加息的预期。

亚洲市场回落，因以芯片为主的交易所领跌

MSCI 亚太股市指数下跌 2.7%，MSCI 所有国家世界指数下跌 0.4%。

日本日经 225 指数下跌 3.3%，东证指数下跌 1%。澳大利亚 S&P/ASX 200 指数下跌 0.4%，新西兰 NZX 50 指数上涨 0.7%，新加坡海峡时报指数下跌 0.2%。

中国沪深300指数和上证综指分别下跌0.88%和0.98%。印度 Gift Nifty 50 指数期货下跌 0.2%。

与此同时，澳大利亚 10 月份通胀加速至 4.9%，调整后的平均通胀升至 3.8%，超出预期，尽管澳大利亚央行官员戴维·雅各布斯 (David Jacobs) 称，在五次加息、将现金利率提升至 4.85% 的 18 年高点后，金融状况受到限制。

布伦特原油下跌 1.2%，至每桶 90.30 美元左右，交易商权衡供应增加与霍尔木兹海峡附近船只遭受的袭击升级。

阿里巴巴子公司被列入黑名单加剧了地区人工智能供应链的担忧

芯片制造商在新一轮抛售中首当其冲。 SK海力士下跌9.1%，三星电子下跌9.3%，LG Innotek下跌5.5%。台积电跌7.6%，富士康跌9.2%，大立光电跌1.4%。日本铠侠 (Kioxia) 下跌 15%，村田 (Murata) 下跌 16.1%。

中国科技股也走弱，北方华创科技下跌8.5%，寒武纪科技下跌3.7%，中芯国际下跌2.6%。 Z.AI 和 MiniMax 分别下跌 8.5% 和 7.1%。

由于担心先进计算产品可能被转移，美国商务部还将包括阿里巴巴新加坡子公司 Apex Enterprise Solutions 在内的七个东南亚实体列入其出口管制黑名单。

阿里巴巴称此次上市是错误的，否认 Apex 转移了受控芯片，并表示将寻求法律选择。

此举可能会使区域云和人工智能运营商访问先进计算基础设施变得复杂，同时加强对涉及跨境半导体供应链的中介机构的审查。
